messages.author: 1167fabdc1ff491d
messages.subject: Extended Bayesian Skyline plot
parts:
Hi everyone!

I am trying to run extended bayesian skyline plot with my data, but for this I need two things:
1) I need to know how many snps there are in each fragment in order to choose the fragments with higher number of SNPs;
2) Save each fragment as a different fasta or nexus file.

Can anyone help me with this?

Thank you in advance

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Extended Bayesian Skyline plot
parts:
Hi Jessica,

 

This sounds like a great future feature for a future dartR package. I would be happy to help but if I am not mistaken you need to know somehow on which fragment each SNP is. Todo so you either have this information already or you need to blast your SNPs (with the surrounding sequence) to a reference genome. So the question is do you have already the information on which fragment the SNPs are?

 

I wanted to implement a dartR function to do that quite some time, but did not come around to do so. Do you have this kind of data?

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.author: 1167fabdc1ff491d
messages.subject: Re: [SUSPICIOUS MESSAGE] Re: [dartR] Extended Bayesian Skyline plot
parts:
Hi!
Thank you so much for the answers Dr.  Gruber and Dr. Georges!

Dr. Gruber, I am following this tutorial: http://www.emilianotrucchi.it/images/EBSP_RADseq_tutorial.pdf and for what I understood I just need to know how many SNPs there are in each fragment just to cluster in the analysis the fragments with the same number of SNPs.
However, I gave up this step as  it appears that all my fragments only have one SNPs.... Although I am not filtering by secondaries SNPs, I think that some how the other filters are deleting the fragments with more SNPs.

Dr. Georges, I tryed the command  table(gl@other$locmetrics$CloneID)  but it returned the message < table  of extent 0 >

I used the command gl.subsample.loci to randomly set 50 SNPs and changed the code of the function gl2fasta not to concatenate the SNPs, but it only added a space among the SNPs in each individual row. So I am manually creating separated fasta file for each SNP, but it is demanding too much time.
There is any code capable of creating separated files for each SNPs containing all the individuals?

Thank you!
Cheers
Jessika

Hi Jessika,

can you try

table(table(gl@other$loc.metrics$AlleleID))

gl is your genlight object. This should give you a table on the number of snps within each 69 bases (if you have dart derived data).

Cheers, Bernd
